newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota governor proposes $1.9 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota governor proposes $1.9 bln budget.

text.p: South Dakota Governor William Janklow proposed a $1.9 billion all-funds fiscal 1997 budget Tuesday that continues a 20 percent property tax cut.
Jim Soyer, a spokesman for Janklow, said the budget included state aid payments to local governments to make up for revenues lost to the property tax cut.
He explained that in the current fiscal year, the first year the tax cut plan was implemented, the state made direct payments of about $80 million to local governments.
The budget for the fiscal year that begins July 1 also called for $18.2 million more in spending on education, with $13.1 million of the amount slated for local school districts.

"We must make sure we have excellent educational opportunities, safe communities and, of course, do whatever we can to help those who really need our help in their daily lives," Janklow said in a news release.
The governor's budget also allocated $4.3 million more for crime protection and $13.3 million for social services needs.
Janklow said the addition funds were made possible through state employee cuts and a projected $17.9 million increase in state revenues next year.
Soyer said legislators are scheduled to take up the proposed spending plan in January.
